summary:
I judged the merged tree (4b0016f) that the merge out will produce: uat with SL-076, plus SL-077's attempt 3. Nothing is wrong.

What changed:
- src is identical to the attempt-1 commit; `git diff --stat 98faaae HEAD -- src` is empty.
- SL-076 brought in only tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 (Invoke-HarnessRaw now reads just the leaf of the kept scratch path) and tests/bugs/SL-076-ScratchKeptPath.Tests.ps1. Neither hard-codes a count that SL-077 moves: I grepped both for 28/29/42/43/55/56, PathOpens, F24-F26, P24 and SL-077 and found nothing.
- Attempt 3 added the five names to both yaml patterns and both twin-Fact patterns. It reworded the texts to 'the named path-taking entry points', stating that an unlisted name passes; no text left in the tree claims every path-taking call. It also replaced the count Fact's third copy of the name list with FactPatterns, which reads the twin Fact's source.

I attacked FactPatterns:
- Its literal regex is character for character the `$literal` that eng/rules-parity.ps1:235 uses, so it reads the copy parity compares against the yaml.
- It unescapes doubled quotes correctly; the count Fact passes, and its expected list includes the GetDiskFreeSpaceExW entry-point string, which only the second pattern can match.
- Every layout change it cannot read fails loudly (missing Fact, fewer or more than two patterns, no group 1), never open.
- The alternation order is safe: CreateFile[AW2]? before CreateFileTransacted and FindFirstFile(Ex)? before FindFirstFileName backtrack, so the full name is captured.

On the merged tree I ran:
- Full default suite: 414/414 passed.
- rules-parity -ExpectFacts 12: AGREE, 29 patterns.
- RuleCases C-001 to C-005: each 'All checks held.'
- Fitness check: all 62 rules hold.

The builder reports C-006 to C-014, the harness (56/56) and SL-076's bug test as held. Those need the engine backend path, and I did not re-run them.

This slice has looped, and no single stage can see it from where it stands. Build attempts 2 and 3 were both sent by code-review, both changed no src, and each widened the same enumerated name list (m2, R2-m2, then m1). A name list can always be one entry short. The texts now say so, and the builder correctly points further widening at the deferred process-wide SetErrorMode follow-up rather than another lap.

Second round: Nothing new to file. I went through the new reader, FactPatterns, looking for any input that makes it read a narrower rule and still pass, and found none. Every layout change it cannot read makes the count Fact fail loudly:
- A trailing comment after a pattern literal. rules-parity strips comments first, but FactPatterns does not, so that literal is skipped, the count becomes 1 and `patterns.Count == 2` fails.
- An exception path written on a line of its own. It would be read as a third pattern and fail the same check.
- `[Fact]` on the same line as the method, or an expression-bodied Fact. Either way the method is not found, `at < 0`, and the Fact fails.

Parts that hold:
- CRLF line endings, a BOM and tab indentation are handled by ReadAllLines and `\s*`.
- Doubled quotes are unescaped correctly, as the passing GetDiskFreeSpaceExW entry-point match shows.
- The loop stops at the first literal ending `);`, so it never reads into the next Fact.
- The yaml `because` uses `''` correctly, and Fitness parses the entry.
- The count Fact's own line reader over Kernel32.cs is unchanged since my earlier rounds. Its two contrived evasions (a call split across a line break, and a `//` comment followed by U+2028) are still not worth filing.

For whoever picks up the deferred process-wide SetErrorMode follow-up: `CreateFile[AW2]?` does not match `CreateFile3(`. I believe CreateFile3 is a path-taking API added in the Windows 11 24H2 SDK, and this machine runs build 26200, but I did not confirm it here. I am not filing it. The rule's texts now say it holds only the names it lists, and another widening lap is the loop I named last round.

The `using` scope at SynchronousIoCancel.cs:352 and Kernel32.cs:170 is unchanged. The restore and nesting Facts passed in 414/414.
Scope outermost in Open, one pair per open. Unchanged.
Repro Fact passed.
Repro Fact (worker) and the AProbeOnThisThread Theory passed.
EveryFolderTheScanOpensIsOpenedWithTheBoxOff passed.
BothRoutesOfAFolderOpenRunWithTheBoxOff passed.
Theory preset 0 passed.
Theory preset 0x2 passed.
Theory preset 0x1 and NestedScopesUnwindInOrder passed.
AFailedOpenRanWithTheBoxOffAndGivesTheModeBack passed.
ACancelledOrThrowingOpenGivesTheModeBack passed.
The dedicated-thread Fact passed.
TheVolumeReadRunsWithTheBoxOffAndGivesTheModeBack passed.
Counting-rule classes passed within 414/414.
Kernel32.cs:206-224 and :108-115 are unchanged (Obsolete(error) ctor, IsArmed, wrapper refusal).
Private CreateFileW and the token wrapper are unchanged.
The twinned yaml entry, the ArchitectureRulesTests Fact and plants F24-F26/P24 are present. Parity AGREE at 29 patterns; RuleCases C-001 to C-005 held on the merged tree.
Superseded by the wider list now in the yaml and the Fact.
No Fact depends on pool-thread reuse.
BothRoutes asserts KeptLastAccess per fixture.
One pair per open; the timing is builder-reported.

The eng/read-window.ps1 -DefaultErrorMode launcher is unchanged. In the prior lap I re-ran it on E:\ and F:\ (ERRORMODE 0x0, EXIT 0, RootUnreadable/21). src and the exe are unchanged since, and the builder re-ran it on E:\ this attempt.
The .taad/fitness.yaml `because` and the ArchitectureRulesTests doc state that the compiler holds SynchronousIoCancel.cs and review plus the count Fact hold Kernel32.cs. The count Fact passes.
Both patterns (call with [AW]?, and entry-point string) are in the yaml and the twin Fact; plant F26 is present; parity AGREE at 29 patterns.

GetCompressedFileSize[AW]?, FindFirstFileName[AW]?, FindFirstStream[AW]?, GetFileInformationByName and CreateFileTransacted[AW]? are in both must_not_match patterns in .taad/fitness.yaml and in both verbatim patterns in ArchitectureRulesTests.PathOpensGoOnlyThroughTheGuardedOpen. The texts say 'the named path-taking entry points'; a grep for 'every path-taking' or 'Any other path call' outside .taad/slices finds nothing. Fitness holds, parity AGREE.

FailCriticalErrorsTests.Kernel32MakesOnlyThePathCallsThatRunInsideTheScope no longer holds a literal. FactPatterns finds the Fact via nameof and reads its verbatim pattern lines with the same regex as eng/rules-parity.ps1:235 (`^\s*@"((?:[^"]|"")*)"\s*(,|\);)\s*$`). It asserts exactly two patterns, each with group 1, and it passes on the tree.

cases.evidence: Repro Fact, call 1 on the scan thread; unchanged and passing.
Repro Fact (probe worker) and the direct-Probe Theory.
BothRoutes with KeptLastAccess true and false.
AFailedOpen: error 5 folder, missing folder, missing file.
ACancelledOrThrowing: cancel in the bracket, refused Enter, throwing AfterCall.
The dedicated-thread form review m3 accepted.
Volume Fact through the BeforeVolumeRead hook.

The end-to-end read-window.ps1 -DefaultErrorMode run on real empty removable drives E:\ and F:\ (child mode 0x0, RootUnreadable/21, no timeout). I re-ran it in the prior lap; src and the exe are unchanged since.
Handle-based calls after media removal remain out of scope, a design open question for a person.

drift: Loop: build attempts 2 and 3 were both caused by code-review, changed no src, and each widened the same enumerated path-API name list. The texts now admit the list is not exhaustive. Any further widening belongs to the deferred follow-up on handle-based calls and a process-wide SetErrorMode, not to another review lap on this slice.

No new departure from the design in this attempt. The builder's choice, reading the twin Fact's source rather than asserting a literal occurs in it, is one of the two options the m2 disposition offered.

Carried forward, unchanged:
- The empty-drive check has not been shown able to fail: the pre-fix exe was never run with -DefaultErrorMode, because that needs a person present to dismiss the box.
- The design record still has would_force_resynthesis: true on per-open cost, and the key_decision's rejection grounds for a process-wide call are not yet restated.
- At merge, watch for the engine re-adding a '# settled by SL-077' block under the design's prose rule name (HF-008).
unreviewed: .taad/slices/SL-076/*.json and .taad/slices/SL-077/*.json brought in or changed by the merge and the build: stage records, not code.
